review.summary: The repair works for pages that use the server boundary. The page reads the scalar query values on the server and passes them through the retry context, so the native hidden fields and the JS request body use the same values. That avoids reading `window` during server rendering, so there is no hydration mismatch. A failed native submission saves valid values inside the existing encrypted draft, and the retry page restores them before falling back to the current query. Empty hidden values fail the format check and are dropped the same way on save, so retry saving stays consistent. The context still checks `formId`, so a boundary for one form can't leak its values to another form, and the `sourcePath` redirect carries no source values. There are two issues. (1) The `/form/[slug]` boundary call does not pass `query.submitted`, unlike the three other pages, so the verified-success state may be lost there. This is only a regression if that line used to pass it, which needs checking. (2) The JS path for older callers without a boundary uses `URLSearchParams.get()`, so a repeated query field keeps its first value instead of being dropped. That contradicts the claim that repeated fields are omitted consistently. As already declared, no-JS submissions from those older callers still send empty source values; that is outside the authorized repair. Final lint, typecheck and browser runs are still pending, and no findings here does not mean they passed.

findings.issue: The `/form/[slug]` boundary call passes `formId`, `sourcePath`, `attributionQuery` and `retry`, but not `submitted: query.submitted`. The other three updated pages (`/p`, `/lp`, `/lp/[stepPath]`) all pass it, and this page's `searchParams` type also declares `submitted`.
findings.evidence: `registrationRetryBoundary({ formId: form.id, sourcePath: `/form/${slug}`, attributionQuery: query, retry: query.registrationRetry })`. Inside the boundary, `verifiedRegistrationSubmission(formId, sourcePath, undefined)` therefore always returns false, so `retry.submitted` is false and `LeadForm` starts in `idle`.
findings.impact: If this line used to pass `submitted`, it is a regression. After a successful native (no-JS) submission redirects to `/form/<slug>?submitted=verification_required`, the page would show an empty form instead of the verified success message and LINE follow-up. Users could then submit the same registration twice. The diff doesn't show whether `/form` handles `submitted` some other way.
findings.recommended_fix: Add `submitted: query.submitted` to the boundary call, matching the other entry pages. If `/form` deliberately handles `submitted` elsewhere, document that and confirm the context still sets `submitted: true` for a verified result cookie.
findings.required_test: Browser/integration test: submit natively (no JS) on `/form/<slug>` and follow the redirect to `?submitted=verification_required` with a valid result cookie. Assert the success message renders and the form is hidden. Then use a forged `submitted` without the cookie and assert the form stays idle.

findings.issue: In the JS fallback for callers without a boundary, `URLSearchParams.get()` returns the first value of a repeated parameter. `registrationAttribution` therefore receives a valid string and keeps it. The server boundary receives an array for the same URL and drops the field.
findings.evidence: The server path gets `string | string[]` from Next `searchParams`; the array fails `safeParse`, so the field is omitted. The legacy path passes `query.get("ref") ?? undefined`, so `?ref=a&ref=b` produces `referralCode: "a"`.
findings.impact: The same URL produces different source values depending on whether the page has a boundary. This contradicts the stated rule that invalid or repeated fields are omitted consistently, and it lets an ambiguous link still claim a source on legacy pages. Referral eligibility is still decided by the API, so there is no direct way to bypass authorization.
findings.recommended_fix: Build the fallback input with `getAll`. For each key, pass `undefined` when there are no values, the single string when there is exactly one, and the array when there are several. Alternatively, convert the whole query to the `RegistrationAttributionQuery` shape before calling `registrationAttribution`.
findings.required_test: Unit test: calling the legacy query-to-attribution conversion with `?ref=a&ref=b&lp=x&lp=y` gives `{}` for those fields, matching `registrationAttribution({ ref: ["a","b"], lp: ["x","y"] })`. Browser test: on a page without a boundary, the JSON body for that URL contains `referralCode: null` and no `landingPageId`.
